observations: All tested PutScalingPolicy calls returned HTTP 200 Success. Labels containing denied refer to caller CloudWatch IAM permissions, not to an outer Application Auto Scaling denial.

Creating target-tracking policies succeeded with implicit absence and explicit deny of caller cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm, and with implicit absence and explicit deny of caller cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms. Baseline describe calls immediately observed one policy and both managed alarms in each case.

CloudTrail records three forwarded caller PutMetricAlarm AccessDenied events: implicit absence during creation, explicit deny during creation, and explicit deny during update. Each denial names an alarm subsequently created successfully by AWSServiceRoleForApplicationAutoScaling_ECSService/AutoScaling-ValidateScalingPolicy. The exact alarm correlations are retained below.

An existing target-tracking policy changed TargetValue 50 to 75 under explicit PutMetricAlarm deny, then to 80 under explicit DescribeAlarms deny, then to 60 with all tested permissions. Each update replaced both managed alarm names; state snapshots show the new thresholds, not preservation of the prior configuration.

No outer target-tracking update failure was induced by the requested caller CloudWatch permission variations. Therefore rollback/atomic preservation after an outer denied update is not established by this capture; child PutMetricAlarm denials were recovered and final policy/alarm state was complete.

DeleteScalingPolicy succeeded with no caller CloudWatch permissions and with explicit caller DeleteAlarms deny. In both cases the immediate baseline snapshot showed no policies or managed alarms and one retained scalable target.

DeregisterScalableTarget succeeded with no caller CloudWatch permissions and with explicit caller DeleteAlarms deny. In both cases the immediate baseline snapshot showed no policies, alarms, or scalable targets.
Deleting the actual zero-task ECS service under the no-CloudWatch role removed its target, target-tracking policy, and managed alarms by the first subsequent baseline snapshot.

Observed final-policy and target cleanup DeleteAlarms calls used the existing ECS Application Auto Scaling linked role/AutoScaling-ManageAlarms. Some replacement-alarm deletions during policy updates used forwarded caller authority. CloudTrail actors, request alarm names, and event IDs are preserved rather than treating every DeleteAlarms as the same path.

No forwarded DescribeAlarms call under an owned assumed role was observed in the bounded CloudTrail capture. Permission simulations confirm implicit/explicit deny variants, but event absence alone does not establish whether an internal DescribeAlarms authorization check exists.
All seven owned inline IAM policies and roles were deleted; each final GetRole returned NoSuchEntity. No existing global linked role was changed or deleted.

Final ECS service and cluster are INACTIVE with desired/running/pending counts zero. Running/stopped task lists and subnet network-interface list were empty. Subnet and VPC describe calls returned not-found after deletion. Task definition deletion was accepted and final status remains DELETE_IN_PROGRESS; physical purge is not claimed.
